name: AMANDA
full_name: Antarctic Muon and Neutrino Detector Array
summary: The predecessor of IceCube demonstrated high-energy neutrino detection in deep Antarctic ice and measured atmospheric-neutrino samples before integration with the growing IceCube array.
physics_targets: High-energy point sources and diffuse neutrino fluxes
detection_principle: Photomultiplier modules frozen into vertical boreholes recorded Cherenkov light. Upgoing muon reconstruction used the Earth to reject the much larger downgoing cosmic-ray-muon background.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: Berkeley Lab reports AMANDA was turned off in August 2009.

timeline.event: Deeper AMANDA-B and AMANDA-II strings installed.

collaboration.name: AMANDA Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Principal neutrino sample
key_parameters.value: Atmospheric muon neutrinos from roughly 100 GeV to 10 TeV

results.summary: The atmospheric-neutrino spectrum and tests of nonstandard propagation were published; source searches found no confirmed excess.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
